name: Fantasy & sports picks
blurb: Free pick'em games, survivor pools, bracket challenges and fantasy leagues run by media companies and leagues. This is where free entry is most often written into official rules — and where the prize money is most often modest and shared.
read: Highest volume of free-entry cash in the ledger. The winners are operator-run pick'em games (ESPN, CBS) because the rules explicitly say no purchase necessary and the prize tables are published. Treat fantasy mini-leagues and tipster contests as advertising, not prizes.

name: Tech & data competitions
blurb: Machine-learning competitions, hackathons and federal prize challenges with published cash pools. Free to enter on most platforms; the cost is your compute time and a working submission.
read: Largest verified cash pools per event ($65k–$2M) and the best fit for an AI-assisted workflow. The bottleneck is not entry, it is finishing a competitive submission before the deadline.

name: Creative contests
blurb: Photography, writing, design and humour prizes judged on a submission. Some are genuinely free to enter; many charge an entry fee or require a paid membership.
read: Mixed. Photographic and literary awards are usually free to enter and pay real money, but they take months and usually require original work — several explicitly ban AI-generated entries.

name: Forecasting tournaments
blurb: Scored probability forecasts with sponsor-funded prize pools. Nothing is staked, and there is a dedicated track for automated/bot forecasters.
read: The cleanest free path in the entire ledger: no fee, no stake, published pools, and an explicit bot track that suits an agent workflow.

name: Skill tournaments
blurb: Head-to-head and multiplayer skill games, from solitaire cash apps to esports ladders. Free rooms typically pay gems; cash rooms usually charge an entry fee.
read: Mostly a trap. Free rooms pay non-withdrawable currencies, and the handful of real free-entry cash events are small and require genuine game skill.

name: Market competitions
blurb: Paper-trading and demo-account contests scored on simulated returns. Usually free, because brokers use them as marketing.
read: Free to enter, but the prizes are frequently trading plans or gift cards rather than withdrawable cash, and many are lead-generation funnels for prop firms and brokers.

name: Free pool & league platforms
blurb: Tools that run office pools and survivor leagues. The platform does not fund a prize; your pool does.
read: Not prize sources. Useful only if you are running a pool and want a free host.

name: Trivia competitions
blurb: Live or asynchronous quiz contests. Free daily plays exist; cash prizes usually require surviving a long elimination ladder.
read: The thinnest category in the ledger — two entries, neither with a verified cash path at the time of audit.

name: Directories & listings
blurb: Places that list many competitions at once. Use them to discover events, then verify each event against its own official rules.
read: Useful research hop, never a source of truth: a directory listing is not the operator's rules.
